title: PIP Policy Version Conflict at 90-Day Review
scenario_text:
**ServiceNow HR Case — CASE0012847**
Type: Performance Improvement Plan | Employee: Marcus Rivera, CNC Machinist III (Plant 2) | Manager: Tom Kowalski
Opened: Sep 12, 2025 | PIP Issued: Sep 15, 2025 | 90-Day Review Due: Dec 15, 2025
Case notes (Sep 15): 'PIP issued per Progressive Discipline Policy v3.2, Section 4.1. Three documented quality incidents in 60-day window. Final written warning stage per CBA Article 12.'
Case notes (Nov 3): 'Rivera filed ADA accommodation request — see CASE0012901. Investigation hold NOT triggered per ER guidance.'

**SharePoint — /policies/hr/progressive-discipline (Page version 8, published Nov 1, 2025)**
Section 4.1 (revised): 'PIP duration extended to 120 days for represented employees. Employees on active PIPs as of the effective date transition to the new timeline unless the PIP document explicitly states a fixed duration.'
[Version 7, published Mar 2023, stated: '90-day PIP for all employees regardless of classification.']
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @d.hartley, Oct 14]: 'Legal says transition language was added at union's request during CBA side letter negotiation. Only applies to Article 12 grievance-eligible roles.'

**Microsoft Teams — ER Internal (Nov 8, 2025, 2:44 PM)**
@tom.kowalski: Natalie — does the new 120-day thing apply to Rivera? His PIP doc says '90-day improvement period' explicitly.
@natalie.brennan: Checking with labor counsel. The PIP doc language might make it fixed.
@tom.kowalski: 👍
[No further messages in thread]

**Outlook — From: jennifer.liu@ironforge.com (outside counsel) To: natalie.brennan@ironforge.com (Nov 12, 2025)**
Subject: RE: Rivera PIP timeline question
> Natalie — the transition clause uses 'unless the PIP document explicitly states a fixed duration.' Rivera's PIP says '90-day improvement period' but does not use the word 'fixed.' My read: the word 'explicitly' requires express language about immutability, not just a stated duration. The 120-day timeline applies.
>
> That said, if Tom already communicated Dec 15 verbally to Rivera, changing it now creates a past-practice argument the union could use.

**ADP — Marcus Rivera (Emp #4412)**
Classification: Hourly/Non-Exempt | Bargaining Unit: IAM Local 1847 | Seniority Date: 2018-03-04 | Current Status: Active
Recent Pay Action: Step increase processed Oct 1, 2025 (automatic per CBA wage scale)

**Microsoft Teams — #plant2-ops (Dec 2, 2025, 7:15 AM)**
@tom.kowalski: Heads up team, Rivera's PIP review is the 15th. I've already told him that's the date.
@shift-lead-jenkins: 👀
@tom.kowalski: It is what it is
question: It is now Dec 5, 2025. What is the correct PIP review timeline for Marcus Rivera, and what is the primary risk if the wrong date is applied?

contributor.name: Natalie Brennan
contributor.title: Employee Relations Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Performance improvement plans, workplace investigations, union grievance handling, progressive discipline policy application

choices: The 120-day timeline applies per the revised policy's transition clause, but proceeding on Dec 15 is defensible because Tom already communicated that date to Rivera, creating a past-practice issue.

The 120-day timeline (Jan 14, 2026) applies because outside counsel confirmed the PIP language does not meet the 'explicitly fixed' threshold, and the primary risk of using Dec 15 is a grievance under Article 12 for failure to follow the CBA side letter.
The 90-day timeline (Dec 15) applies because the PIP document explicitly states '90-day improvement period,' satisfying the carve-out in the revised policy.
The PIP should be paused entirely due to the pending ADA accommodation request in CASE0012901, making the timeline question moot until the interactive process concludes.
